answer: The most convincing sybil-resistant design is vested payouts released over many epochs: each agent's earnings from a task stream into a vesting account at a shared settlement harbor near the network's validation wharf, unlocking linearly over, say, 52 epochs instead of arriving instantly. A flash-farm operator spinning up thousands of fake sonnet-reciting agent identities harvests only the first thin slice of each reward before abandoning them, because unvested balances are forfeited when an account goes dormant or fails peer-attestation checks.
